answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, where transition mass is damped by each edge’s credibility. A sybil cluster can accumulate influence only by receiving substantial flow from honest nodes; if its external boundary is sparse, its conductance is low, so mixing and escape probabilities remain limited. Min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap aggregate voting weight, while atlas, violet, and inlet attestations cannot bypass the bottleneck.
